metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Moldova

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Moldova and selected international comparisons, based on the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically provides sampling weights (and replicate weights) to support population-representative estimates and correct uncertainty quantification. However, this factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable names or whether replicate-weight procedures were used in the reported figures. For analysts reproducing these estimates from microdata, the recommended approach is to apply the official PISA student/sampling weights and the associated replicate weights (if available) for standard errors and confidence intervals, and to use the OECD-provided scaling/scoring outputs for creative thinking.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking proficiency and related associations; it does not provide an analysis section that specifies plausible-value (PV) generation/combining rules or a missing-data strategy for an empirical model. While PISA achievement is typically based on PVs, this factsheet reports already-scaled international results and does not document PV handling or missing-data procedures. Therefore, the PV and missing-data handling details are not reported in the provided text, representing a reporting gap for methodological replication.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Moldova’s analytic sample as 6,235 students in 265 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 28,900 15-year-olds (an estimated 97% of the total population of 15-year-olds). The creative thinking results are based on the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment administered to 15-year-olds; the factsheet does not further describe additional exclusions beyond the stated completion of the assessment.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Moldova performed on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking test, which measures the ability to generate, evaluate and improve ideas. The test contains 32 open-ended tasks spanning three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) and four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Moldova’s mean creative thinking score is 24 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average of 33. About 49% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency), while 9% are top performers at Levels 5–6. The factsheet also reports that 30% of the variation in creative thinking is uniquely explained by mathematics performance, and documents within-Moldova gaps by socio-economic status and gender, plus associations between creative mindsets and performance. It includes cautions for some comparison countries/economies due to unmet PISA sampling standards.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (descriptive reporting) rather than an empirical ML study with a specified predictive modeling pipeline. As a result, there is no model training, no reported ML algorithms, no PV-combining or missing-data handling procedure, and no student-level analytic design described beyond the reported Moldova sample size and the PISA assessment structure. The extraction therefore leaves ML-specific fields empty and focuses on the assessment design and reported performance benchmarks.
